title: Rollout rehearsal runbook and chaos simulation draft
content:
Purpose and scope:

Purpose: practical rehearsal checklist + small-scale chaos simulation recipes to validate cross-functional canary and A/B rollout choreography before any wide exposure. This doc is intentionally tactical — scripts, measurement definitions, comms templates, and failure scenarios we can run in a 2–4 hour dry run.

Scope: hosted API + Dedicated routing + Console traffic slices. NOT covering private air-gapped installs in this draft (we'll adapt later).

Motivation / quick notes to self:
- We keep seeing flaky signal alignment (metrics vs UX) during real canaries. Need repeatable rehearsal to catch blindspots.
- Goal: catch ops-level regressions, signal plumbing gaps, and human comms breakdowns before customer traffic.
- Target audience: PMs, SRE, Observability, Serving Runtime, Solutions Eng, Oncall.

Core roles for a rehearsal (who's in the room):
- Release Lead (RL): coordinates timeline, authorizes stop/continue.
- Traffic Steward (TS): controls slice weights, issues traffic switches.
- Observability Lead (OL): watches telemetry dashboards, runs queries, fields alarms.
- Model Steward (MS): validates output quality and can trigger rollback.
- Oncall / SRE: executes infra remediation, scaling, and failovers.
- Comms owner: posts Slack + incident channel messages.

Runbook outline (high level):
1) Preflight (30–45m): config sanity checks, preregistered dashboards, burn-in tests.
2) Baseline capture (15m): capture production-ish baseline metrics on the slice we plan to touch.
3) Micro-canary (10–20m): direct 1% traffic -> new variant, observe signals.
4) Chaos scenario(s) (20–40m each): inject simulated failure(s) (latency spike, instance OOM, KV cache miss storm, model mismatch).
5) Decision checkpoint (5m): RL + OL + MS decide continue/rollback.
6) Escalation + remediation (as needed).
7) Postmortem mini-retro & checklist updates (15–30m).

Preflight checklist (must clear all):
- Release config checked into rw-rollouts repo (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- Canary slice IDs reserved and isolated (no external traffic).
- Alert channels and paging paths pre-confirmed with oncall.
- Dry-run keys and quotas set (to avoid accidentally billing infra).
- Observability queries saved (IDs + short descriptions).
- Test prompt corpus uploaded to eval job for quality checks.
- Stakeholders invited to the rehearsal call (calendar invite + Slack pinned).

Signals to watch (telemetry contract):
- latency.p50_ms, latency.p95_ms, latency.p99_ms (ms)
- request.error_rate (5xx + L7 failures) (fraction)
- model.confidence_drift (KL or cosine distribution distance vs baseline) (unitless)
- rerank.n_asks_to_human (count)
- generated_content.hallucination_rate (hand-labeled quick evals in the 50-sample probe) (fraction)
- cost_per_token_estimate_usd (moving average)
- kv_cache.hit_rate (fraction)
- autoscale.actions (count)

For each metric we need: query id (saved), baseline, alert threshold (warning/critical), expected direction, and suggested mitigation play.

Example metric contract entries (put into dashboards before run):
- latency.p95_ms: baseline 280ms, warning if >400ms sustained 3m, critical if >700ms for 1m -> mitigation: cut canary weight, scale pool, enable fallback model.
- request.error_rate: baseline 0.002, warning if >0.01 sustained 5m, critical if >0.03 any 1m -> mitigation: immediate rollback to previous model, enable degraded path.
- generated_content.hallucination_rate (probe): baseline 0.05, warning if >0.12 on probe sample, critical if >0.20 -> mitigation: pause rollout, run larger eval, revert.

Rehearsal scenarios (minimal set):
A) Slowdown cascade (network latency + kernel scheduling)
- Goal: validate latency SLO detection + traffic steward response
- Template steps: inject synthetic 200–500ms upstream latency from model pool (simulate using delay proxy), run 1% -> 5% -> 10% ramp, watch latency.p95 & p99, ensure automatic fallback triggers at configured thresholds, ensure RL receives alerts.
- Expected: p95 jumps -> warning -> TS reduces weight -> OL confirms fallbacks engaged -> RL approves continue or rollback.
- Play artifacts: delay proxy recipe (rw-rollouts/sim/delay-proxy.sh), dashboard link (saved query id).

B) Cache eviction storm
- Goal: ensure KV cache miss storms are visible and autoscale handles token-case burst.
- Template steps: generate synthetic traffic that deliberately busts prefix cache (unique long-context prompts), watch kv_cache.hit_rate drop and token cost spike.
- Expected: cost_per_token_estimate_usd rises, autoscale.actions increases. Verify cost alerts and an operator can throttle non-critical routes.

C) Model-quality regression (silent)
- Goal: validate detection of quality regressions through small probe and human-in-loop escalation
- Template steps: flip in a model variant with a known subtle regression (e.g., shorter answers, lower factuality), run 50-sample probe (scripted), have MS perform quick label pass using the evaluation form.
- Expected: generated_content.hallucination_rate increases above warning -> MS escalates, RL decides to halt.

D) Partial region outage (regional fallback)
- Goal: test smart routing & fallback to replica region or lower-cost variant without user-visible downtime
- Template steps: simulate instance group in region eu-west-1 failing health checks -> smart-router should route new requests to other regions or fallback models; verify telemetry and SLO adherence.

Concrete decision tree (text form) - simplifies roll/stop logic:
1) If any critical alerts fire (latency critical / error_rate critical / hallucination critical) -> immediate pause exposure and rollback to previous stable variant.
2) If multiple warning-level signals (>2 warnings across independent signal families for >5m) -> pause ramp and run extended probe (200 samples + runbook).
3) If single warning with plausible mitigation (cache miss, autoscale pending) -> allow TS to reduce weight by 50% and observe 5–10m.
4) If no signals after 20m of 10% exposure -> consider continuing ramp (RL approval).

Slack + Incident channel templates (copy+paste):
- Opening message (start of rehearsal):
  "@here Rehearsal START: RW roll #RW-1345. Slice: canary-ctx-skim-001. Leads: RL=Maya, TS=Ethan, OL=Priya, MS=Lucas. Timeline: 60–90m. Do not route real customers to these slices. If you are paged, reply with 'ACK rehearsal' and join #rollout-rehearsal."

- Alert escalation message (auto-template):
  "Alert: latency.p95_ms crossed CRITICAL threshold for canary-ctx-skim-001. RL please advise. Link: <dashboard-url>. If no response in 2m, TS will auto-reduce weight to 0%."

- Rollback announcement (manual):
  "Rolling back canary-ctx-skim-001 -> reverted to model v2025-01-18. TS reduced weight to 0% at 10:14 UTC. Postmortem owner: @Priya. Paging SRE for follow-up."

Data collection and quick eval steps (probe):
- Use eval harness at rw-eval/probe-run to execute 50-shot probe. Store results in /tmp/probe-outputs/<timestamp>.csv. Key cols: prompt_id, prompt_text, model_version, tokens_generated, rating (1–5), hallucination_flag (0/1), notes.
- Manual labeling can be done in parallel (MS + 2 raters) with 60m SLAs.

Chaos simulation tooling notes:
- We prefer lightweight tools that don't require infra-level chaos monkey for rehearsals. Use traffic proxy scripts, mock delay injectors, and controlled config flips. Production-grade chaos (instance terminations) only in dedicated chaos windows with SRE co-approval.
- Scripts live in github: rollout-sim/ (see linked_artifacts).

Post-rehearsal mini-retro checklist:
- Did alerts surface the issue in time? yes/no/notes
- Were dashboards clear and actionable? yes/no/notes
- Did any human steps take >10m unexpectedly? list
- Which runbook items are ambiguous? list
- Action owners + deadlines (add to RW-1345).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a compact smoke-test that simulates hallucination-type regressions without human labeling? (Priya investigating synthetic adversarial prompts)
- Can we wire a cheap LLM-based semantic-drift detector to flag distributional changes in embeddings? (RFC: OL to prototype)
- Add explicit play for 'degraded cost-control' (someone should be able to throttle routes automatically).

Small appendices (links / snippets):
- quick probe CLI: rw-eval probe --corpus=sanity-50.json --model=canary --out=/tmp/probe-$(date +%s).csv
- weight control example (Traffic Steward CLI): rw-rollouts traffic set-weight --slice canary-ctx-skim-001 --weight 0.01
- rollback example: rw-rollouts release rollback --slice canary-ctx-skim-001 --target v2025-01-18 --reason "rehearsal-critical-latency"

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc is intentionally operational and a bit messy. We should turn successful rehearsal checklists into a runbook template in Confluence and a set of saved run scripts in the rollouts repo.
- After first 3 rehearsals we'll convert high-confidence thresholds to Prometheus alert rules / Grafana panels and make rollback CLI a one-click action in the Console.

-- Maya
